title: Japanese for Trains in 9 Comic Scenes | Guess, Listen, Say It (Travel Japanese)
lead: Finding the station, buying a ticket, changing trains and getting out at the right exit, in nine comic scenes. Guess first, then listen twice and say it.

intro.title:
Japan trains
**9 phrases**
intro.say: Nine scenes on Japanese trains. Guess each line before the answer.

phrases.label: Finding the station
phrases.when: Looking for a station? Ask like this.
phrases.tip: Swap Shinjuku for the station you want. Doko desu ka means where is it.
phrases.scene: On a city sidewalk near a station entrance, Jiwoo holds a folded paper map and asks the station attendant standing by the entrance; the attendant points down the street with a gloved hand; Minjun looks around behind Jiwoo.

phrases.label: Buying a ticket
phrases.ja: 切符はどこで買えますか？
phrases.pron: Kippu wa doko de kaemasu ka?
phrases.ko: Where can I buy a ticket?
phrases.when: Need a ticket but can't find the machines? Ask this.
phrases.tip: With an IC card like Suica, you can skip the ticket and just tap in.
phrases.scene: In the station concourse, Jiwoo looks around, confused, and asks the attendant; the attendant gestures toward a row of ticket machines with blank glowing screens.

phrases.label: Which platform
phrases.ja: 渋谷行きは何番線ですか？
phrases.when: Not sure which platform to go to? Ask this.
phrases.tip: Yuki means bound for, and bansen means platform number. Platform three is sanban-sen.
phrases.scene: Past the ticket gates, Jiwoo holds a small paper ticket and asks the attendant; the attendant holds up three fingers and points toward a staircase leading up to a platform.

phrases.label: Does this train go?
phrases.ja: この電車は渋谷に行きますか？
phrases.pron: Kono densha wa Shibuya ni ikimasu ka?
phrases.ko: Does this train go to Shibuya?
phrases.when: Not sure it is the right train? Ask before you get on.
phrases.tip: For a bus, say basu instead of densha: kono basu wa Shibuya ni ikimasu ka.
phrases.short: Check you are on the right train
phrases.scene: On the platform beside a silver commuter train with its doors open, Jiwoo points at the train and asks the attendant, who nods with a smile; Minjun waits by the door.

phrases.label: How many stops
phrases.ja: 渋谷はいくつ目の駅ですか？
phrases.when: Want to know how many stops until yours? Ask this.
phrases.tip: Ikutsu-me means which number in order. The answer sounds like mittsu-me, the third one.
phrases.scene: On the platform, Jiwoo counts on her fingers with a curious look and asks the attendant, who counts on her gloved fingers too.

phrases.label: Changing trains
phrases.ja: 乗り換えはどこですか？
phrases.when: Changing lines and lost? Ask this.
phrases.tip: Norikae means transfer. Big stations show signs in English too.
phrases.scene: In a wide underground passage, Jiwoo pulls a small suitcase and asks the attendant, who points toward a corridor with a pictogram arrow sign showing a train symbol.

phrases.label: Getting off
phrases.when: Train too crowded to get out? Say this.
phrases.tip: Say sumimasen, orimasu, and people will make way for you.
phrases.scene: Inside a crowded train car, Jiwoo squeezes toward the open door with one hand raised politely; faceless commuters on the right step aside; Minjun follows close behind her.

phrases.label: Finding the exit
phrases.when: In a big station, ask for your exit like this.
phrases.tip: Big stations have many exits. West is nishi, south is minami, north is kita.
phrases.scene: In the station concourse after the gates, Jiwoo looks at a compass app on her phone (no writing) and asks the attendant, who points to the right with a gloved hand.

bonus.label: After getting help
bonus.when: Finally, say this to someone who helped you find the way. They will love it.
bonus.scene: Outside the station exit in daylight, Jiwoo bows slightly with a relieved smile and Minjun gives a thumbs-up; the attendant bows back.

outro.title: Recap: **9 phrases**
outro.say: All the phrases are in the description. Tell us in the comments how many you got right. Subscribe so you don't miss the next one.
